calls.title: The Missing Email
tags: Mixed-up details: a wrong birth year
calls.about: An older client never got the email about the doctor's appointment her case manager set up, and gives the wrong birth year at first.

key.v: Gloria Benton, existing client
Yes: full name, DOB 07/05/1960 (she said 1950 first; the VA asked again), DOL 09/03/2026
Never got the confirmation email for her appointment with Dr. Herrera, Bayview Orthopedics, Thu 11/12/2026 at 1:00 PM; the email on file was missing a dot
Gave her the clinic's address and phone; corrected email (g.benton60@mail.com) noted on the file; message to Mara Quintero (Case Manager) to resend the confirmation today

calls.handled: Didn't accept a birth year that didn't match: asked again instead of guessing, then found why the email never arrived and gave her the address on the call.

transcript.text: Harbor & Pine Injury Law, this is Oscar. How may I help you today?
Hi, yes, my name is Gloria Benton. I have an appointment with a doctor, with, oh, I don't know if I can say it. It's a long name. Doctor Her... Herrera?
That's all right, Ms. Benton, I'll look that up for you. First I just need to verify your file. Can you give me your date of birth?
July fifth, nineteen fifty.
Thank you. Hmm, I'm not finding a match with nineteen fifty. Could you give me the year once more?
Oh! Sixty. Nineteen sixty. I'm sorry, I said fifty. Nineteen six-zero.
No problem at all. July fifth, nineteen sixty. And the date of your accident?
September third. This year.
Thank you. Gloria Benton, date of birth July fifth, nineteen sixty, accident September third, twenty twenty-six. You're verified. Now, one moment while I pull up your appointment.
Okay. I see your appointment with Doctor Herrera at Bayview Orthopedics on Thursday, November twelfth, at one PM. Your case manager, Mara, set that up.
Yes. That's the one. She said they would send me an email with all the particulars, the address and all that, but I never got it.
I'm sorry about that. Let me check the email we have for you. I have g benton six zero at mail dot com. Is that right?
No, no. It's g dot benton, with a dot. G, dot, B, E, N, T, O, N, six zero, at mail dot com.
Thank you. So that's g, dot, benton, six zero, at mail dot com. That explains the missing email. I'll note the correct address on your file. In the meantime, would you like the clinic's address now?
Yes, please. Let me get a pen. Okay.
Bayview Orthopedics, twenty-one fifty Bayshore Boulevard, suite three hundred, in Tampa. Their phone is five five five, zero one six, seven seven zero zero.
Twenty-one fifty Bayshore, suite three hundred. Okay, I have it.
Perfect. I'll also ask Mara to resend the confirmation to your correct email today. Is this the best number to reach you?
Yes, this is my home phone. Five five five, oh one nine, two oh four seven.
Five five five, zero one nine, two zero four seven. Is there anything else I can help you with, Ms. Benton?
No, that's all, dear. Thank you so much.
You're welcome, Ms. Benton. Take care. Goodbye.

calls.title: Third Time Calling
calls.about: A client in pain calls again about the letter his pain clinic needs before it will book his injection.

key.v: Andre Wallace, existing client
Yes: full name, DOB 02/15/1985 (read back, as he said it fast), DOL 07/22/2026
His third call about the Letter of Protection for Gulf Coast Pain Center, which won't book his injection without it; the request is with Devin Shaw, due tomorrow
Tried a warm transfer to Devin Shaw (Records Coordinator, on another call); urgent message for a callback today; the repeat calls noted on the file

calls.handled: Apologized once and acted: checked the file at once, tried to reach the person handling it, and passed on an urgent message with the whole story.

transcript.text: Harbor & Pine Injury Law, this is Oscar. How may I help you today?
Yeah, I'm calling to get an update on the letter for my pain doctor. I called last night. I called yesterday morning too. This is the third time.
I'm sorry you've had to call more than once. Let me check on that for you right now. Can I have your full name and date of birth?
Andre Wallace. Two fifteen eighty-five.
Thank you, Mr. Wallace. That's February fifteenth, nineteen eighty-five?
Yes.
And the date of the accident?
July twenty-second.
July twenty-second, twenty twenty-six. You're verified. One moment while I look at your file.
Okay. I see the request for a letter of protection to Gulf Coast Pain Center. It's been assigned to our records coordinator, Devin Shaw, and it's due tomorrow.
Tomorrow? They won't book my injection until they get that letter. I'm in pain every day. I can't keep waiting on this.
I understand, Mr. Wallace, and I'm sorry you're in pain. Would you like me to try to connect you with Devin now?
Yes. Please.
Please hold for one moment.
[on hold]

Thank you for holding, Mr. Wallace. Devin is on another call right now. I've sent him an urgent message: that this is your third call, that the clinic won't book your injection without the letter, and that you need it sooner than tomorrow. I've asked him to call you back today. What's the best number for him?
This one. Five five five, oh one two, five five eight three.
Five five five, zero one two, five five eight three. And is there a time that's better for you?
Anytime. I'm home.
Got it. I've noted all of this on your file, so whoever you speak with next will know the whole story. Is there anything else I can help you with?
No. Just, please, get it done.
I understand. Devin will call you today. Thank you for your patience, Mr. Wallace. Goodbye.

calls.title: Which Office?
calls.about: An imaging centre's front desk wants a fax number for the firm's other office and doesn't say who the records are for.

key.v: Kayla Jensen, front desk, Sun City Imaging (a medical provider)
(555) 011-6630; the firm's fax confirmed: (555) 010-4410
A provider, not the client: the patient named as Tomas Reyes; nothing about a file confirmed
Faxing an MRI report; asked for the Brandon office's number (all offices' calls come to reception and all faxes go to the records department)
Confirmed the fax number; told her to fax it attention Devin Shaw (Records Coordinator) with the patient's name and DOB on the cover sheet; Devin told to watch for it

calls.handled: Asked who was calling and what the fax was about before routing it, confirmed the number she had, and confirmed nothing about the patient.

transcript.text: Harbor & Pine Injury Law, this is Oscar. How may I help you today?
Hi, I need the phone number for your Brandon office. I'm faxing something over and I want to make sure they get it.
I can help with that. All of our offices' calls come here, and the faxes for every office go to our records department. What fax number are you sending it to?
It looks like I have five five five, oh one oh, four four one oh.
Yes, five five five, zero one zero, four four one zero. That's the correct fax number.
Okay, great. Can I put it to the attention of someone at the Brandon office?
Sure. May I ask who's calling, and what the fax is about?
Oh, sorry, I didn't say. This is Kayla, from the front desk at Sun City Imaging. It's an MRI report for one of our patients. Tomas Reyes.

Thank you, Kayla. I'm not able to confirm anything about a file on this call, but you can send it to the attention of Devin Shaw, our records coordinator. Please put the patient's full name and date of birth on the cover sheet, so it gets to the right place.
Devin Shaw. S, H, A, W?
That's right. And may I have your last name and a callback number, in case Devin has a question about the report?
Jensen. J, E, N, S, E, N. And our number is five five five, oh one one, six six three zero.
Kayla Jensen, Sun City Imaging, five five five, zero one one, six six three zero. I'll let Devin know the report is on its way. Is there anything else I can help you with?
No, that's it. Thank you!
Thank you for calling, Kayla. Have a good day.

calls.title: Just Confirming
tags: Short call: every step still counts
calls.about: A client calls to confirm tomorrow's meeting with her attorney: a quick call where it's easy to skip a step.

key.v: Nicole Avery, existing client
(555) 013-9126 (confirmed as still current)
Yes: full name, DOB 05/28/1983, DOL 04/09/2026
To confirm her meeting with Atty. Celeste Harbor tomorrow, Thu 10/29/2026 at 4:00 PM, at the office
Confirmed the meeting from the calendar; the call noted on the file

calls.handled: Kept it quick without cutting corners: verified her before reading out the appointment, and checked the callback number on file.

transcript.text: Harbor & Pine Injury Law, this is Oscar. How may I help you today?
Hi, I'm just calling to confirm my appointment for tomorrow.
Sure, I can check that for you. Can I have your full name and date of birth?
Nicole Avery. May twenty-eighth, nineteen eighty-three.
Thank you. And the date of the accident?
April ninth.
Nicole Avery, May twenty-eighth, nineteen eighty-three, accident April ninth, twenty twenty-six. You're verified. One moment.
I show your meeting with Attorney Celeste Harbor tomorrow, Thursday, October twenty-ninth, at four PM, here at the office.
Yep, that's it.
Perfect. And is five five five, zero one three, nine one two six still the best number for you?
Yes, it is.
Great. I've noted your call on the file. Is there anything else I can help you with?
No, that's all. Thank you.
You're welcome, Ms. Avery. See you tomorrow. Goodbye.

calls.title: No Ride Tomorrow
calls.about: A client whose usual ride fell through can't get to tomorrow's doctor's appointment and asks to reschedule.

key.v: Darnell Pryce, existing client
(555) 014-7751, taken before the transfer
Yes: full name, DOB 03/13/1994, DOL 05/30/2026
His veterans' shuttle can't take him to tomorrow's follow-up with Dr. Herrera, Bayview Orthopedics (10/29/2026, 10:30 AM), and he has no car; wants to reschedule
Warm transfer to Mara Quintero (Case Manager, ext. 610), briefed on the internal line: the verification, the appointment, the reason and the callback number

calls.handled: Took the callback number before the hold, and briefed Mara fully so the client didn't have to tell his story twice.

transcript.text: Harbor & Pine Injury Law, this is Oscar. How may I help you today?
Hi, uh, good afternoon. My name is Darnell Pryce. I'm a client. I'm calling about my, um, my doctor's appointment tomorrow.
Good afternoon, Mr. Pryce. I can help with that. First, can I have your date of birth?
March thirteenth, nineteen ninety-four.
Thank you. And the date of the accident?
May thirtieth. This year.
Darnell Pryce, March thirteenth, nineteen ninety-four, accident May thirtieth, twenty twenty-six. You're verified. What's going on with tomorrow's appointment?

So usually the veterans' shuttle takes me, but, uh, they just called and nobody's available to drive me tomorrow. And I don't have a car right now, since the accident. Is there any way I can reschedule?

I'm sorry about that. I see your follow-up with Doctor Herrera at Bayview Orthopedics tomorrow, October twenty-ninth, at ten thirty AM. Your case manager, Mara Quintero, coordinates your appointments, so let me connect you with her. Before I do, what's the best number in case we get disconnected?
Five five five, oh one four, seven seven five one.
Five five five, zero one four, seven seven five one. Please hold for a moment while I get Mara.
Okay. Thanks.
[on hold]
Hi Oscar, it's Mara.

Hi Mara. I have Darnell Pryce on line one. He's verified: date of birth March thirteenth, nineteen ninety-four, accident May thirtieth, twenty twenty-six. His ride to tomorrow's ten thirty with Doctor Herrera fell through, and he has no car, so he'd like to reschedule. His callback is five five five, zero one four, seven seven five one.
Thanks. I'll take him, and I'll see if we can set up transportation too.
Mr. Pryce? Thank you for waiting. I have Mara on the line for you.
Hi Darnell, it's Mara. Oscar filled me in. Let's get you a new date, and let's talk about getting you a ride.
Thank you. I really appreciate it.

calls.title: Mom on the Line
calls.challenge: Background noise and an unauthorized caller
tags: Family member not on the file
calls.about: A client's mother calls from a busy house, upset: her son is back in hospital and she wants to know about his case.

key.v: Linda Carter, mother of the client Jordan Carter
Not the client and not authorized in writing: nothing shared or confirmed, not even whether there is a case
Jordan was admitted to Tampa General on 10/27/2026 after a fall (his knee); she asked when the settlement is coming
Urgent message passed on internally (to Jordan's case manager, Mara Quintero) for someone to call Jordan directly today; told Jordan can call himself to authorize her; noted on the file

calls.handled: Stayed calm and kind through the noise and the frustration, confirmed nothing about a case, said why nothing could be shared, and still took the urgent message.

transcript.text: Harbor & Pine Injury Law, this is Paolo. How may I help you today?
Yes, hi, my name is Linda Carter, my son Jordan is your client, and I need to know what is going on with his case, because nobody is telling us anything.
Grandma! He took my tablet!
Not now, baby! Sorry. Sorry.
That's all right, Ms. Carter. I can hear this is a stressful time. I'll do my best to help you. May I ask, are you calling on someone's behalf today?

Yes, for my son, Jordan Carter. He fell again, because of his knee, and he's back in the hospital since last night. Tampa General. And I want to know when the settlement is coming, because the bills are piling up.
I'm so sorry to hear Jordan is in the hospital. Please give me one moment.

Thank you for waiting, Ms. Carter. For privacy, we can only discuss a case with the client, or with someone the client has authorized in writing, so I'm not able to share or confirm any information. I know that's frustrating to hear.
I'm his mother! I'm the one driving him to all his appointments.

I completely understand, and I can hear how much you're doing for him. It's to protect Jordan's privacy. What I can do is take a message and pass it on right away, so the right person can reach Jordan directly. If Jordan would like you to be able to speak with us, he's welcome to call us himself, and we'll explain how.
Okay. Okay. Yes, please do that.
Grandma, the dog is out!
Thank you. What's the best number to reach you, in case she needs to?
Five five five, oh one eight, six six one two.
Five five five, zero one eight, six six one two. And so I have it right: Jordan was admitted to Tampa General last night, October twenty-seventh, after a fall, because of his knee. Is that correct?
Yes. That's right.
Thank you, Ms. Carter. I've passed your message on as urgent, and someone will reach out to Jordan today. Is there anything else I can help you with?
No. Thank you. I'm sorry I yelled.
Please don't apologize. I hope Jordan feels better soon. Take care, Ms. Carter.
